analyses.name: fixed_threshold_extraction_effect
analyses.purpose: Isolate count-extraction changes with the archived thresholds unchanged.

analyses.name: corrected_calibration
analyses.purpose: Evaluate the corrected implementation with the original calibration rule on corrected tuning negatives.

requirements: Freeze code, runtime, BAM/BAI identities, source profiles, tracks, site order and all output paths before extraction.
Reextract observed counts for both calibration and replicate-2 controls; never reuse affected observed arrays.
Reuse only checksum-valid sequence log-bias profiles and expected DWM tracks with verified site order; rescale each strand expectation to corrected strand totals.
Preserve every original task and motif locus. Report invalid windows, zero counts and underpowered tasks explicitly.
Use identical corrected observed counts for both scoring arms. Keep original validity support as a diagnostic and report any changes separately.
Freeze both methods' recalibrated thresholds before scoring replicate 2. Do not select between analyses based on control outcomes.

For historical-rule calibration retain the original eligibility rule; additionally report zero or unavailable DWM expectation among calibration negatives. Unqualified baseline calibration cannot establish relative safety.
Report absolute candidate rates on all finite sites and informative sites, plus paired relative rates only where DWM expectation is positive and normalized observed profile shapes agree.
Report archived versus corrected baseline-comparable memberships and count differences; do not hide denominator changes behind a rate comparison.
Require false-positive rate and Wilson upper bound at most 0.05 and paired increase over DWM at most 0.01; retain residual-shape and observed-profile disagreement checks.
Retain every historical artifact unchanged. Verify nested outputs independently before interpreting a successful process exit.
Replicate 2 is previously examined candidate-screen evidence; it cannot establish final untouched safety, functional uncertainty coverage or occupancy-leakage exclusion.
